subject: Intermittent empty responses in production (Novus Retail) - update
messages:
From: John Davies <john.davies@novusretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Empty completions observed in production - sample attached

Hi Sean,

We're seeing intermittent responses from the Redwood API where our app receives an empty completion (200 OK, empty 'choices' array). It happened across three user sessions this morning between 08:40 and 09:05 PT. I attached a HAR and the request body for one of the requests.

Can you confirm whether this is a platform issue or if something on our side could cause the body to be stripped? Customers are noticing failures in checkout flows. We're on model: rwd-3-small, region us-west-2, tokenization/streaming enabled.

Thanks,
John
Senior Engineering Manager
Novus Retail

Attachments: client_har_capture.zip (archive), novus_request_sample.json (json)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: John Davies <john.davies@novusretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Empty completions observed in production - sample attached

Hi John — thanks for the quick report and the attachments. We're triaging this now. Initial ask: can you share a request ID for one of the failed requests if available? That will let us pull the exact routing and traces.

What we'll do next:
- Check our request logs and trace for the timestamp window you provided
- Reproduce against rwd-3-small with the same request body and streaming settings
- Validate any intermediate proxies or client-side transforms (we'll include a short checklist below you can run while we dig in)

Quick troubleshooting checklist (client-side):
1) Confirm your SDK version (we know a 0.9.x bug could affect streaming framing)
2) If you use a proxy/load balancer, ensure it doesn't drop or modify chunked transfer encoding
3) Try a non-streaming single-shot request with identical body and note if the empty result persists

I'll follow up once we have traces. If you can paste a request ID that will speed things up.

—Sean
Sr. Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Novus Retail: triage notes and reproduction attempts

Team — summary of what I ran overnight after John sent the HAR and sample request. Including logs in the attachment redwood_trace_1012.log.

Observations:
- We pulled all requests from 2026-10-10 08:30–09:15 PT for Novus account and for the model rwd-3-small. No server-side 5xx errors were observed; all relevant API responses from the serving cluster were 200 and contained well-formed JSON.
- Two request traces from the same route show small latencies but no token-generation errors; the token pipeline completed and we emitted an empty 'choices' array only if the upstream payload was empty (i.e., our generator produced zero tokens because the request length was 0 after decoding).
- Reproduction: I replayed the exact request body from novus_request_sample.json against the same model and settings (streaming on and off) using our internal test harness — responses were normal and non-empty across 25 runs.
- We compared the HAR to our ingress logs: the request bodies we received match the sample you provided in size and checksum. There is one instance where the client connection was closed early (FIN) from an external IP around 08:49 PT which correlates with one reported empty result; the server emitted a partial stream but the client likely consumed 0 bytes.

Preliminary conclusion: no evidence of a runtime bug in Redwood that would systematically produce empty completions. The most likely causes are: premature client-side connection termination, an edge proxy that buffered and then forwarded incomplete payloads, or an SDK framing issue on Novus' side.

Action items:
- Karthik: can you run a deeper check on the LB logs for the c-10.23.5.x IP and confirm whether we saw any upstream resets? (INF-4422)
- Marissa: I'll coordinate a short joint test with Novus (we ask them to run a non-streaming request and provide the request-id).
- Monica: pls prepare a short customer note template offering a one-time usage credit for the affected window while we confirm root cause.

I'll draft the customer-facing closure once Karthik completes the LB check.

—Sean
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: John Davies <john.davies@novusretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Update: Novus Retail intermittent empty responses — conclusion and next steps

Hi John,

Thanks again for the samples and for working with us. We completed an internal review and here are the findings and recommended next steps.

What we checked:
- Full request/response traces from Redwood for the window 2026-10-10 08:30–09:15 PT (attached redwood_trace_1012.log).
- Load balancer and gateway logs for your tenant route (Karthik validated; no server-side error state or runtime failure).
- Reproduction against rwd-3-small using the exact request payload and streaming toggled — no deterministic empty completions produced.

Conclusion: We did not find a platform defect that would cause systematic empty completions. The most probable explanation is a client-side connection termination / network proxy behavior that resulted in a truncated receive on Novus' side. Specific indicators: we observed one connection close (client FIN) aligned with a single empty result report, and all server-side traces show complete generation when a full body was received.

Recommended next steps for Novus:
1) If possible, capture the request-id for any empty events — we'll pull traces immediately.
2) Temporarily disable streaming for the checkout flow for 24 hours as a mitigation; our internal tests showed identical payloads succeeded in non-streaming mode when the client fully received the response.
3) Have your infra team check the proxy/load-balancer logs for any upstream resets or timeouts around the reported times.

Compensation: As a gesture while we closed this loop, we've credited your account with 10k tokens for the affected window. Monica will follow up with the exact billing note.

If you want, we can run a joint screen-share next week and reproduce against your exact SDK environment — Marissa, can we schedule a 30-minute test?

Thanks — let me know if anything else shows up. We're standing by to re-open investigation if you get request IDs or further traces that suggest server-side truncation.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_trace_1012.log
